translation: He had gone to Malwa together with Guru Gopaldas in Samvat 1867. There the two became separated, and Gopaldasji passed away in Ujjain. There, on the bank of the river Shipra, stands the Gopal Mandir, which houses the image of Morli Manohar (the flute-charmer, Krishna). While teaching Jivanji, Gopaldasji had said that the true Morli Manohar was the cowherd of Gokul, who carries one beyond the Vedas of Brahma [i.e., surpasses even scriptural knowledge through pure devotion]. Because this temple in Ujjain belongs to Gopaldasji, who spoke these words, and because it is also the place where Gopaldasji gave up his body, Ujjain is a place of merit (punya sthali). Moreover, when Jivandasji returned from the Himalayas, he came to Ujjain. He must have remembered his guru, and, thinking also of his beloved devotees, he came here. Around Ujjain, in places such as Chanderiya and Khediya, his devotees lived; one of them, a woman named Jyotibai, had also come to Ujjain to shop. She spotted Jivanji there, and, overjoyed [almost beside herself], went and brought the other devotees to him. Thus this Ujjain is a place of merit (punya sthali) that recalls the meeting of guru and disciple, and disciple and guru.
